description: Golden reference for PEEC-inductance on a 3-turn loft coil (multi-turn, tight pancake) with explicit lead bars.
rationale: Locks in the cross-section-centroid chain method PLUS lead-bar-aware chain augmentation for loft-of-profiles solids whose terminal leads are straight cylindrical bars (CYLINDER faces, no intermediate CIRCLE samples).  Kubota's 3turncoil geometry has 2 lead bars at y=+/-12.5mm extending 60-61mm in +/-X from the helix end to the lead terminal.  Pre-2026-05-13 the NN-chain saw only the lead cap CIRCLE edges (no body samples), giving a chain like: lead_inner_cap_A -> [helix 314 segs] -> lead_inner_cap_B -> lead_outer_cap_B (61mm single seg) -> lead_outer_cap_A (25mm fake U-bend through air).  This produced L = 421.84 nH.  Since 4.44.0 the chain is augmented after NN-chain by _augment_chain_with_lead_bars: long segs on a lead axis are subdivided into N intermediate stations; fake air-jumps at chain ends are dropped; missing lead bodies are prepended/appended.  Result: L = 426.30 nH on both the in-repo 3turnCoil_work_coil.step and W:/kubota/3turncoil.stp.  The chain now correctly starts at one lead's outer tip (port +) and ends at the other lead's outer tip (port -).  Note on the 426.25 nH baseline cited below: this is the LEGACY .jou-path PEEC reference (the original Cubit-journal-driven PEEC route that v4.13.0 replaced with STEP-only).  There is NO closed-form analytical solution for a 3-turn pancake + lead bars; the 426.25 figure was the value the .jou path produced (see docs/release_notes_v4.7.0.md: 'sibling 3turnCoil.jou -> L = 426.245 nH'), kept as a sanity baseline when comparing the new STEP-only path against the prior pipeline.  Earlier rationales calling it 'analytic' or 'analytic-equivalent' were inaccurate -- both 426.25 (.jou-PEEC) and 426.30 (STEP-PEEC + lead-aware) use the same PEEC filament solver, so the 0.02% agreement reflects topology equivalence across pipelines, not validation against an independent method.  CONVERGENCE STUDY 2026-05-13: (c) PEEC n_peri sweep 8 -> 16 -> 24 -> 32 -> 48 -> 64: L = 423.89 / 426.30 / 428.08 / 429.26 / 430.72 / 431.55 nH, MONOTONIC.  Richardson extrapolation (1/n_peri linear) gives PEEC continuum L_inf approx 434 nH.  R_coil (Dowell) drops 0.3974 -> 0.3859 mOhm, also converging.  (b) BEM-A mesh sweep (ngsolve.bem dense LU, Weggler EFIE + SIBC): 4028 tris (cap 6/6, A_src -17%) -> 432.57 nH; 5938 tris (cap 6/6, A_src -17%) -> 417.56; 9848 tris (cap 14/14, A_src -6%) -> 412.18.  BEM-A is NOT MONOTONIC.  The 4028-tri value 432.57 coincidentally matches the PEEC continuum (~434), but the trend at 5938/9848 drops away.  (a) Attempting 14972 tris (cap 24/24, A_src -1%) failed: dense LU on 37429^2 saddle K = 22 GB OOM in scipy.linalg.solve; MINRES with rtol=1e-8 ran 107 min and grew memory to 61 GB without converging (probably stalled near indefinite saddle without preconditioner).  Production-grade BEM-A at >10k tris needs HACApK/FMM acceleration with block-diagonal preconditioner — out-of-scope for this commit.  CONCLUSION: PEEC continuum well-established at ~434 nH.  BEM-A continuum NOT pinned down: 3 data points are non-monotonic, the 14972 anchor point is unreachable with current dense implementation.  Production PEEC value 426.30 nH (n_peri=16) is retained as the panel default — it is 1.8% below the PEEC continuum, deliberate trade-off for ~1 s solve time.  R_coil disparity (PEEC 0.39 vs BEM-A 4.7 mOhm) is mesh-independent and points to a formulation-level disagreement (likely Dowell vs SIBC interpretation of wire-radius surface impedance).

sample.comment: File lives on Kubota's 100号機 share (W:) not in-repo (4 MB).  Test skips if unavailable rather than duplicating the binary in the repo.  Coordinates in metres (CLAUDE.md m-only policy).  The in-repo sibling src/radia/panels/samples/3turnCoil_work_coil.step has the same physical geometry and produces the same L (verified 2026-05-13).

physics.coil: 3-turn pancake coil R_avg~35mm r_wire=3.15mm, 2 lead bars 60-61mm at y=+/-12.5mm

expected.note_2026_05_20: Default solver switched to proximity-aware iterative PEEC (peec_proximity.solve_proximity_iterative).  R 3.6752 -> 4.4793 mOhm, L 430.14 -> 431.32 nH.  proximity_factor = 4.4793 / 3.6763 = 1.218 (iterative-vs-self-only R ratio at 150 kHz on this geometry).  Sweep verifies the factor is constant ~1.20-1.22 across 1 kHz - 1 MHz -- the structural ceiling of perimeter PEEC, which captures surface-Leontovich proximity but NOT transverse eddy loops in the wire interior.  The LCR hi-tester measurement was ~15 mOhm; the gap 4.48 -> 15 mOhm is most plausibly lead/contact resistance (5-50 mOhm typical for 2-terminal probes at low Ohm).  4-terminal Kelvin re-measurement on the coil terminals would confirm.  See docs/esim/R_MISMATCH_PEEC_VS_BEMA.md and docs/peec/VOLUME_PEEC_DESIGN.md.  Cross-check: pass --no-peec-proximity to calc_inductance.py to get the self-only Bessel values listed above (3.6763 mOhm / 430.24 nH).
expected.note_2026_05_19: (historical) R_coil first lifted from R_DC (0.39 mOhm at any frequency) to full Bessel AC (3.6752 mOhm) by injecting Zs_fil per filament (cylinder_ac_impedance for a round wire) into solve_loop_bundle.  L_coil shifted 426.30 -> 430.14 nH because Z_cyl(omega).imag/omega includes the internal-inductance Bessel term.

regression_guard.comment: Hard band centred on the legacy .jou-path PEEC reference 426.25 nH (+/-3%).  Historical baselines: 2026-04-21 longest-edge gave L=4.78 nH; GeomType string compare missed enum; NN chain without tangent continuity doubled path length.  2026-04-28 (4.14.0): _collect_circle_edge_centers recovered cross-section centroids from semicircle pairs of a UNITE'd STEP, giving 421.84 nH.  2026-05-13 (4.44.0): _augment_chain_with_lead_bars repairs lead-related NN-chain artifacts (single-seg lead bodies, fake U-bends, missing lead bodies), giving 426.30 nH.  Convergence study 2026-05-13: PEEC n_peri sweep 8/16/24/32/48/64 -> 423.89/426.30/428.08/429.26/430.72/431.55 nH (monotonic, 1/n_peri-linear extrapolation -> L_inf ~ 434 nH).  BEM-A mesh sweep 4028/5938/9848 tris -> 432.57/417.56/412.18 nH (NON-monotonic).  14972-tri BEM-A unreachable: dense LU saddle K = 22 GB OOM, MINRES ran 107 min without converging (no preconditioner).  Production PEEC 426.30 nH (n_peri=16) is 1.8% below PEEC continuum -- deliberate trade-off for ~1 s solve time vs ~90 s at n_peri=64.  See rationale for full discussion.  TODO: implement HACApK + block-preconditioned MINRES in coil_inductance_ngsolve.py to enable BEM-A above 10k tris.  Separately: investigate the Dowell vs SIBC R-coil disparity (PEEC 0.39 mOhm vs BEM-A 4.7 mOhm), which is mesh-independent.
